departments.name: Shooter Systems
departments.mission: Own gunplay and combat feel: weapons, ballistics, recoil, hit detection, damage, armour, cover and tactical combat behaviour.

deliverables.name: Weapon and Combat Design
acceptance: Every weapon listed with damage, rate of fire, spread and range numbers
Time-to-kill computed per weapon against each armour class
Counterplay and cover rules stated per engagement range

deliverables.name: Weapon and Damage Systems
acceptance: Every weapon fires, reloads and swaps with no state desync
Hit detection matches the visual model including edge cases
Damage and armour values read from the tuning table only

deliverables.name: Gunplay Review
acceptance: Recoil, audio, VFX and animation cues aligned within the stated window
Measured time-to-kill matches the design table
No weapon is dominant or unusable across the tested skill range

gates: A weapon without computed time-to-kill numbers is rejected
Hit detection diverging from the visual model is a release blocker

departments.name: Civilisation and Strategy Systems
departments.mission: Build the machinery of civilisations and armies: factions, diplomacy, territory, warfare, technology and long-horizon world simulation.

deliverables.name: Strategy Systems Design
acceptance: Faction, territory, diplomacy and warfare rules stated with numbers
Technology tree or research path defined with costs and prerequisites
Victory and loss conditions enumerated
Simulation step budget per turn or tick stated

deliverables.name: Strategy System Implementation
acceptance: Factions act autonomously and observably in a running simulation
Diplomacy and warfare state transitions cannot deadlock
Turn or tick cost measured against the simulation budget

deliverables.name: Strategy Balance Review
acceptance: Simulated matches show no dominant strategy or stalemate loop
AI difficulty tiers show measurable differences
Late-game simulation cost measured within budget

gates: A strategy system without a stated tick cost is rejected
AI opponents that cannot be distinguished by difficulty are rejected

departments.name: Building and Construction Systems
departments.mission: Let players build: placement, snapping, structure, materials, terrain modification, interiors and construction simulation.

deliverables.name: Construction Design
acceptance: Placement rules, grid size and rotation steps stated
Structural support and collapse rules defined with numbers
Build costs, build times and upgrade paths tabulated
Maximum simultaneous structures stated against the performance budget

deliverables.name: Construction Implementation
acceptance: Placement, snapping and demolition work with correct validity feedback
Structures persist through save and load
Terrain deformation matches collision and navigation

deliverables.name: Construction Stress Review
acceptance: Frame cost measured at the maximum permitted structure count
No floating, intersecting or orphaned structures in a stress build
Save and reload of a full build verified once

inputs: models and kits from D06 and D08
gates: A building system with no invalid-placement feedback is rejected
Structures that vanish or duplicate on save/load are release blockers

departments.name: Mining and Resource Systems
departments.mission: Own extraction and processing: mining, destructible terrain, underground generation, ore distribution, refining and crafting economies.

deliverables.name: Geology and Resource Spec
acceptance: Strata, ore types and spawn rules defined with distribution numbers
Extraction rates, tool tiers and yields tabulated
Depletion and regeneration policy stated
Underground generation constraints stated for D29

deliverables.name: Mining and Processing Implementation
acceptance: Mining and terrain deformation work with correct collision updates
Processing and crafting chains produce the specified outputs
Resource counts survive save and load

deliverables.name: Resource Economy Review
acceptance: Resource sinks and faucets reconciled against the economy model
No infinite or degenerate resource loop in a soak simulation
Measured time-to-tier progression matches the design target

gates: A resource system with no depletion or sink is rejected
Terrain deformation that desynchronises collision is a blocker

departments.name: Survival and Simulation Systems
departments.mission: Simulate the pressure of staying alive: needs, health, hazards, wildlife, farming, hunting, crafting and ecosystems.
capabilities: difficulty and accessibility of survival pressure

deliverables.name: Survival Systems Design
acceptance: Every need listed with drain rate, threshold and consequence
Hazard, disease and injury tables with numbers
Crop, wildlife and regeneration cycles stated in in-game time
Accessibility options for survival pressure defined

deliverables.name: Survival Systems Implementation
acceptance: Every need, hazard and consumable behaves to the tables
Wildlife and crops cycle correctly over in-game time
Survival state persists correctly across save and load

deliverables.name: Survival Balance Review
acceptance: Time-to-death from each pressure source measured and inside design range
No resource loop trivialises survival in a long simulation
Difficulty tiers verified as distinct

inputs: world ecology from D03 and D32
gates: A survival need with no consequence or no recovery path is rejected
Balance claims without simulated time-series data are rejected

departments.name: Vehicle Engineering
departments.mission: Build vehicles that feel physical and fair: cars, bikes, trucks, aircraft, boats, tanks, damage, fuel and vehicle AI.

deliverables.name: Vehicle Design and Handling Targets
acceptance: Every vehicle class listed with mass, top speed, acceleration and grip targets
Damage model and failure states defined
Handling reference points stated for tuning comparison

deliverables.name: Vehicle Implementation
acceptance: Every vehicle drives to its handling targets on every surface type
Damage, repair and fuel behave to the design
Vehicle state and position survive save and load

deliverables.name: Vehicle Handling Review
acceptance: Measured acceleration and top speed match the targets
No vehicle can clip through terrain or launch uncontrollably
Handling verified with each supported input device

gates: A vehicle with no measured handling numbers is rejected
Terrain clipping or uncontrollable launch is a release blocker

departments.name: Procedural Generation
departments.mission: Generate worlds that hold up: terrain, caves, dungeons, settlements, missions, populations and dynamic environments.

deliverables.name: Generation Design
acceptance: Every generated layer listed with its algorithm and seed strategy
Guaranteed-content rules stated (what must always exist)
Determinism requirement stated: same seed, same world
Generation budget in milliseconds per chunk stated

deliverables.name: Generator Implementation
acceptance: Same seed reproduces the same world exactly
Generated content always satisfies the guaranteed-content rules
Chunk generation measured within its time budget

deliverables.name: Generation Soak Test
acceptance: At least 100 seeds generated with no unreachable or invalid content
Worst-case generation time measured and within budget
Failure modes documented with reproduction seeds

inputs: terrain and prop kits from D08
gates: A generator that is not seed-deterministic is rejected
Generated content with unreachable areas or missing required content is rejected
